assessment.nobel_worthiness: A new measurement technique in the purest sense: the magic-wavelength optical lattice removes Doppler and recoil shifts while keeping thousands of atoms in the interrogation, giving fractional uncertainties near 1e-18. This reset the limits of what can be measured, and it already enables relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and variation, dark-matter searches and a coming redefinition of the second. Clear, original and with large impact in and beyond physics.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated the first strontium lattice clock; Ye built the highest-performance strontium lattice clocks and drove the precision and comparison programme. This gives a natural two-person prize. Others (e.g. Lemonde, Gill, Ludlow and Hinkley, Bloom) contributed but the core credit is reasonably clear. Interaction with the Hall and Hansch 2005 comb prize and the Wineland ion-clock recognition must be handled in the citation.
assessment.maturity: Mature and independently confirmed by many groups and by clock comparisons across continents and via optical fibre links. Systematic uncertainty has been repeatedly reduced and the practical impact (redefinition of the second, geodesy) is arriving now, so the timing is good.
uncertainties: Whether the committee regards this as sufficiently distinct from the 2005 and 2012 prizes on frequency combs and single-ion control.
Credit to other lattice-clock pioneers such as Ludlow, Hinkley and Lemonde is not in the supplied credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical readout and coherent control of single colour-centre spins (notably NV centres in diamond) at room temperature is a measurement platform that opened quantum sensing of magnetic fields, electric fields, temperature and strain at nanometre scales, with uses from biology to condensed-matter imaging. It also supports solid-state quantum registers and network nodes. Strong in measurement novelty and broad downstream use.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup (first single NV optical detection and magnetic resonance), Awschalom (coherent control and spin physics in diamond and SiC defects) and Lukin (quantum registers, nanoscale sensing proposals and demonstrations) are plausible. Walsworth and others with a strong sensing record are left out, and Gruber/Wrachtrup 1997 versus later contributions is a real allocation difficulty in a field with many contributors.
assessment.maturity: Field is mature and widely reproduced; many commercial sensors exist. Recognition is timely, though a field with so many contributors makes a clean configuration harder.
uncertainties: Choice among four credited names is debatable; Walsworth's contribution to ensemble sensing is arguably decisive.
I rely on memory for the detailed priority history of NV single-spin detection.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions, followed by experimental demonstration of high-fidelity gates, entanglement of many ions and error-corrected operations, established a leading platform for quantum computation. The coherence times, gate fidelities and readout are exactly the kind of measured figures of merit I trust. The ion-trap field is a clear experimental success built on a theoretical proposal.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller for the 1995 proposal, Blatt for the experimental realisation in Innsbruck (Wineland and Monroe also central but Wineland already honoured in 2012 and not in the credited names). The theory-experiment pairing is clean. Overlap with the same three names on B008 means one prize should be framed carefully.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with many independent groups and commercial machines. A prize for the ion-trap quantum gate concept would be timely, but quantum computing credit overall remains distributed across platforms.
uncertainties: Overlap with Wineland's 2012 prize and the question of whether the committee wants a platform-specific prize.
Whether a broader quantum-simulation framing (B008, B047) is preferred over a single hardware platform.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made superconducting qubits controllable and readable through microwave photons in resonators, giving dispersive readout, strong coupling and the transmon architecture on which most superconducting quantum processors rest. A measurement and control technique with great reach in quantum information and in precision quantum sensing.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Wallraff and Schoelkopf are the three natural names: theory with Blais, first strong-coupling experiment with Wallraff and Schoelkopf, with Schoelkopf's Yale group also driving the transmon. Contributions of Devoret, Martinis and Clarke were partly recognised by the recent superconducting-circuit prize, which leaves a possible need to explain how this differs.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation and industrial adoption. A recent prize on macroscopic quantum effects in superconducting circuits may make the committee cautious about a second prize in the same area soon.
uncertainties: Timing relative to the recent superconducting-circuit prize; my knowledge of its exact citation is limited.
Whether the transmon inventors (Koch, Schoelkopf and collaborators) should be included, which the supplied names cannot allow.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum simulation with ultracold atoms in optical lattices (Mott insulator transition, quantum gas microscopes with single-site resolution) provides controllable analogues of Hubbard models and a direct way to measure correlations in many-body systems. Single-site imaging in particular is a real measurement advance. The work links atomic physics to condensed-matter questions in a very clean way.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch, Cirac) for the theory proposal, Bloch and Greiner for the experimental realisation of the Mott transition and the quantum gas microscope. Greiner and Bloch also had the original lattice work with Hänsch. Cirac is listed but I select three; the Mott-transition proposal and experiment are credited to different groups, and Hänsch is outside the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely replicated. The impact on actual solved physics problems is still debated compared with the technique's promise.
uncertainties: Whether the simulation results have yet answered an open question in condensed-matter physics decisively.
Overlap with BEC and optical-lattice prizes already given.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ti:sapphire lasers, Kerr-lens mode locking and semiconductor saturable absorber mirrors made femtosecond pulses a robust, compact tool rather than a dye-laser specialty. These sources underpin attosecond science, frequency combs, multiphoton imaging and ultrafast spectroscopy. An enabling instrument with a pervasive footprint in measurement.
assessment.attribution: Moulton (Ti:sapphire gain medium), Sibbett (Kerr-lens mode locking demonstration) and Keller (SESAM and semiconductor-laser modelocking) each made a distinct decisive contribution. The Strickland-Mourou chirped-pulse prize partly overlaps in application, and credit for Kerr-lens mode locking between the Sibbett group and others needs a careful look.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, in use for decades. If anything the risk is that the impact is by now so widely spread that the discovery is seen as an engineering foundation rather than a single discovery.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as physics discovery or invention that is already covered by the 2018 and 2023 laser prizes.
Spence and others' role in Kerr-lens mode locking is not in the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ground-state cooling and quantum control of mechanical oscillators (sideband cooling, squeezing, entanglement, and optomechanical readout near the standard quantum limit) opened a quantum regime for macroscopic objects and underpin the sensitivity of gravitational-wave detectors and force sensors. Conceptually clean and tied to the limits of measurement.
assessment.attribution: Five credited names; Teufel, Aspelmeyer and Kippenberg are leading figures in cavity optomechanics with distinct experimental milestones, while Cleland (piezoelectric quantum ground state) and Painter (optomechanical crystals) are also decisive. Allocating to three of five is arguable and the field has no single breakthrough.
assessment.maturity: Developing; independent confirmations are many but applications are still emerging. Probably somewhat early for a prize and recognition might overlap with the recent macroscopic-quantum prize.
uncertainties: Five strong contributors with no obvious natural subset.
Practical impact beyond physics remains limited so far.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: X-ray free-electron lasers built on self-amplified spontaneous emission provide femtosecond, coherent, extremely bright X-ray pulses and have opened time-resolved structure determination, single-shot diffraction and nonlinear X-ray physics. A new class of instrument that enables measurements previously not possible, with wide use in chemistry, materials and biology.
assessment.attribution: Pellegrini, Kim and Rossbach cover the SASE theory and early realisation (LCLS and FLASH), but credit also involves Bonifacio, Saldin, Schneidmiller, Yurkov, Madey and the machine builders at SLAC and DESY. The supplied names may not give a fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Mature, with several facilities worldwide and a broad user community. Timing is plausible but credit is diffuse among large collaborations.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among theorists, accelerator builders and facility leaders is disputed or at least unclear.
Whether the committee treats this as a discovery or as an accelerator technology.
